per_window.ps-ns: Reference state (free hTGF-alpha, 2 mM, pH 7.1, 30 °C, no buffer, 500 MHz; RelaxDB source paper doi:10.1021/bi00008a003, full text): dynamic_in_window at the C-terminal tail L48-A50 (S2 < 0.8, two internal timescales), the N-terminal bend D7-C8 and the chain reversals F17-H18, E27-D28, V39-G40, with F23/A31 below 0.85 (J11, E-r1); the rest of the analysed amides have S2 0.8-0.95 (J13, no_evidence_in_window); a presaturated-reference HNOE control shows water saturation transfer inflating apparent NOEs at F5-F15, F23, C34, S36, A41 (J14, artefact_suspected, E-r3). The EGFR-ED paper's abstract calls both termini flexible from methyl relaxation (J1, r3).
per_window.us-ms: Reference state (same sample, single field, full text): exchange detected but unresolved by the single-field rule; 23 of 36 analysed amides carry Rex > 0.5 Hz (D7-C8, T13-H18, T20-K29, C32-V33, V39-G40, E44-H45; 14 amides above 1.5 Hz in the final cycle C, largest R22 4.93, V39 3.81, C21 3.50, L24 3.41 s-1; J12), concentrated at the subdomain interface, which the authors read as interconversion between multiple backbone conformations on the intermediate 15N chemical-exchange (microsecond) timescale with a lifetime between about 1.25 µs and 2.5 ms, candidate mechanisms first-strand dissociation, inter-subdomain hinge bending or disulfide isomerisation; no fitted rate, population or second peak set (J12, E-r2).
per_window.slower_than_ms: No judgment: no row gives a conformational rate slower than milliseconds. The pH-dependent interconversion (J2) has no rate, and the film H/D exchange rates (J5) are solvent-exchange rates, kept in undetermined.
per_window.undetermined: Free ligand: coordinate disorder of the C8-F15 loop among 15 NMR conformers not explained by fast motion alone (J15, E-r4, structure_only); pH-dependent interconversion (J2, r2), partial disorder at pH 3.5 and 30 °C versus pH 6.5 (J3, r9), faster amide exchange than mouse EGF at pH 3.5 (J4, r1), film H/D exchange class rates (J5, r10), all unresolved. Bound states, kept apart from the free domain: EGFR-ED-bound methyl mobility (J6, r3), fast-exchange binding (J7, binding kinetics), IDE-bound D10-Q14 helix-to-strand change in 3E50 (J8, r7), EGFR cryo-EM classes 7SZ5/7SZ7 (J9, r12) and complex MD (J10, r13). Not judged: r4 (1MOX receptor dimer packing in an abstract, no ligand motion), r5 (des-Val-Val construct structure, F15-D47 well defined, pH 6.3), r6 (TGF-alpha 8-50 construct structure), r8 (IDE cleavage-fragment mapping, proteolysis not motion), r11 (human EGF homolog film H/D exchange).

protein_summary.wt_apo_answer: Yes, exchange is detected in the reference state but without a rate or population: in the RelaxDB source sample (free mature human TGF-alpha, 2 mM, pH 7.1 ± 0.1, 30 ± 0.5 °C, no buffer, 500 MHz, single field) 23 of the 36 analysed backbone amides carry 15N exchange broadening above 0.5 Hz (D7-C8, T13-H18, T20-K29, C32-V33, V39-G40, E44-H45; largest at R22, V39, C21 and L24 (3.4-4.9 s-1)), concentrated at the interface between the two subdomains, which the authors read as interconversion between multiple backbone conformations on the intermediate 15N chemical-exchange (microsecond) timescale with a lifetime bounded between about 1.25 µs and 2.5 ms (J12, full text). Single-field Rex can also come from anisotropic tumbling, so the call is 'possible' and a dispersion experiment would confirm; the authors' own intermediate-exchange wording argues against separate peaks. Fast motion sits in the C-terminal tail L48-A50 and the N-terminal bend D7-C8 (J11).
protein_summary.deposition_readback: None: the input lists no BMRB id and outputs/deposition/HTGFA.json does not exist.
open_conflicts: H/D exchange paper (r10): the prose says TGF-alpha beta-sheet exchange is ten orders of magnitude slower than EGF, while Table 1 gives 1.41 x 10-4 versus 1.88 x 10-3 min-1, about one order. Table values are used.

Within the 1995 paper the iterative-cycle text says 25 sites required an exchange term while the final analysis reports 23 (D47's model-6 term rejected; threshold 0.5 Hz); the final 23 are used (J12). The title says 'slow conformational exchange' while the abstract and Results call the regime intermediate 15N chemical exchange on the microsecond timescale; 'slow' there means slower than tumbling, not slow on the chemical-shift timescale.
questions_for_gina: The RelaxDB HTGFA set is presumably Li and Montelione 1995 (doi:10.1021/bi00008a003, pH 7.1, 30 °C, 500 MHz, no buffer; now full text). It detects exchange only as single-field Rex at 23 amides with lifetime bounds of 1.25 µs to 2.5 ms and calls the regime intermediate (microsecond): does single-field Rex count as us-ms exchange for the alternate-APO call (applied here as 'possible' with the anisotropic-tumbling caveat), given that the authors' wording argues against separate peaks?
Does the pH-dependent conformational interconversion in the 1991 structure paper (r2) show two peak sets at one pH, or a shift between pH values? Only the abstract was readable.
protein_summary.buffer_note: The RelaxDB source paper (doi:10.1021/bi00008a003) is now full text (E-rN = HTGFA-HTGFA_20261020201428-rN): 2 mM 15N hTGF-alpha dissolved directly in 90% H2O/10% D2O with 1 mM NaN3, pH 7.1 ± 0.1, 30 ± 0.5 °C, no buffer stated, Varian Unity 500, single field, CPMG 2tau = 720 µs; its abstract-only rows HTGFA-HTGFA_20261020145442-r1 and r2 are superseded and no longer cited. The other free-ligand rows remain abstracts, so their judgments stay unresolved by rule. pH and temperature are part of the state: pH 3.5 at 30 °C and pH 6.5 at 10 or 30 °C are separate states, not one state in exchange. EGFR-, EGFR-ED- and IDE-bound structures are partner-bound states and never enter the wt_apo_answer. The ATR-FTIR data (r10, r11) come from dried films rehydrated with D2O vapour at an unreported temperature and are not comparable with solution NMR. Second reads of the E rows: Claude marked all four ok, Codex left all four unverified, no flags.
